title: arXiv Biology & Biomedicine — 11 November 2026 announcement batch
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart. This is an inferred relevance ranking from checkable evidence, not a readership ranking; arXiv is incomplete biomedical coverage and the report is not clinical guidance.

sections.title: Seven notable papers from the 11 November 2026 arXiv biology and biomedicine announcement batch
sections.text: The strongest cluster is computational protein design and molecular-interaction modeling, with some papers reporting wet-lab validation; other work covers gene-regulatory inference, sequence-based virtual screening, dose-aware molecule selection, bacterial genomics, and spatial expression prediction. The ranking is inferred from relevance and checkable research evidence, not measured popularity.

sections.title: Emergent Biological Capabilities in a Foundation Model for Molecular Interactions
sections.abstract: Bonbon learns protein–ligand interaction representations and reports zero-shot mechanism, binding-site, and bond-type predictions, alongside prospective compound testing.
sections.claimed_contribution: The author reports that one frozen representation supports several zero-shot interaction tasks and transfers to new compounds, with wet-lab hits across nine disease targets in seven protein families.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper says the capabilities are coarse-grained and do not cover residence time, dissociation kinetics, post-binding conformational change, or explicit 3D coordinate recovery. The model is not a toxicity or clinical-efficacy assessment.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Authors report prospective wet-lab testing across nine disease targets and a 61.5% dose-response hit rate; arXiv lists NeurIPS 2026 Main Track Oral acceptance.

sections.title: ProTEUS: A mutation-resolved world model for closed-loop protein evolution
sections.abstract: ProTEUS combines sequence, evolutionary, structural, and assay information to choose protein mutations in closed-loop engineering campaigns.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors present a mutation-resolved model that uses experimental feedback to update protein-activity predictions and guide subsequent choices; they report two enzyme campaigns with variants exceeding tenfold wild-type activity.
sections.unique_caveat: Experimental demonstration is limited to two enzymes and campaign objectives. The paper discloses company-founder/employee relationships and related patent filings; independent replication across proteins and assay settings remains important.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Authors report two multi-objective experimental campaigns on aldehyde dehydrogenase and levansucrase and compare zero-shot and fine-tuned mutation-prediction tasks.

sections.title: Bridging Graph and Pairwise Learning for Gene Regulatory Network Inference from scRNA-seq Data
sections.abstract: scGPL combines global graph structure and local transcription-factor–target interactions to infer gene regulatory networks from single-cell RNA-seq.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors say combining graph-level topology with dynamically sampled local subgraphs improves benchmark gene-regulatory-network inference; they report results on seven datasets and up to a 13.7% improvement over their strongest baseline.
sections.unique_caveat: Benchmark evaluations of inferred networks are not direct experimental confirmation that predicted regulatory links operate in cells; performance depends on datasets and reference labels.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Authors report seven benchmark datasets and up to 13.7% improvement over the strongest baseline; arXiv lists acceptance to Bioinformatics.

sections.title: ANTIOCH-VS: From Sequence to Hits with Modular, Open-Source Ensemble Virtual Screening
sections.abstract: ANTIOCH-VS assembles protein-ensemble generation, docking, consensus ranking, and physics-based triage into a sequence-to-shortlist virtual-screening workflow.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose an open-source workflow that generates docking-ready conformational ensembles and ranked candidate lists from protein sequence without requiring a ligand-bound crystal structure.
sections.unique_caveat: Validation is retrospective and limited to two targets and benchmark decoys. Shortlist enrichment is not experimental confirmation of binding or efficacy; users choose structural features and MSA-depth range.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Retrospective DUD-E tests on JAK2 and ADRB2 report 4/20 and 12/20 top-shortlist hits respectively, against an estimated random rate around 1–2%; code is linked from arXiv.

sections.title: The Dose Makes the Poison: Exposure-Aware Evaluation of Generative Drug Design
sections.abstract: PBPK simulations re-rank PARP1-targeted generated molecules by dose-linked exposure and predicted safety, showing that static molecular-property filtering can miss exposure constraints.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors argue that modeled dose and exposure can change candidate prioritization relative to static predicted potency and toxicity criteria.
sections.unique_caveat: These are PBPK/model-based predictions for PARP1 candidate sets, not measured pharmacokinetics, toxicology, clinical outcomes, or validation of a drug candidate.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Authors evaluate 60 shortlisted candidates from three generative pipelines and report exposure failures, modeled safety risks, and reordered selections; arXiv lists NeurIPS 2026 AI4DD workshop acceptance.

sections.title: Detection of local recombination and mutation hotspots in bacterial genomes using neural posterior estimation
sections.abstract: A simulation-trained neural posterior estimator models gene-specific bacterial mutation and recombination rates and propagates uncertainty into hotspot detection.
sections.claimed_contribution: The method is designed to separate local mutation and recombination signals while carrying posterior uncertainty into hotspot probabilities.
sections.unique_caveat: The estimator is trained under a specified simulation model conditioned on a fixed clonal genealogy; real-data applications demonstrate use, not independent experimental confirmation of inferred hotspots.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Authors test rate recovery on simulations and demonstrate the approach on three bacterial datasets: Bacillus cereus, Staphylococcus aureus, and Escherichia coli.

sections.title: Predicting Single-Cell Spatial Gene Expression from H&E using Pathology Foundation Models
sections.abstract: The authors adapt pathology foundation models to predict single-cell spatial expression from paired H&E images and Xenium 5K measurements.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that task-specific image-model adaptation can recover some spatial expression patterns from routine histology without requiring histology input at inference.
sections.unique_caveat: This is computational inference from paired image/transcriptomic data; the abstract does not establish generalization to independent cohorts, all genes, or clinical use, and reported performance varies by biological context.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Authors report 2.67× mean gene-wise Pearson-correlation increase over a zero-shot baseline, AUROC 0.800 for gene detection, and r=0.643 for spatially variable genes; included under the clear biomedical-research scope exception.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.text: The selected set includes protein models with differing validation settings; computational genomics and transcriptomics papers combining richer structure with explicit uncertainty or evaluation design; and dose/exposure-aware candidate selection. These are recurring topics in this small corpus, not evidence of field-wide trends.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.text: Follow-up directions include independent multi-target protein-model validation; prospective assays for virtual-screening shortlists; perturbation-based checks of inferred gene regulation and robustness to alternate genomic models; measured PK/safety comparisons for PBPK predictions; and external tissue validation for H&E-derived expression.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.text: This batch is notable for protein-model papers that connect computation to some experimental testing, alongside useful but still model- or benchmark-dependent genomics and drug-design methods. Prospective experiments, retrospective benchmarks, and simulations are not interchangeable; no clinical evidence or patient-specific guidance is provided.
